approvalTitle: requirements.md: converting the supply chain diagram to DISL and FBL
content:
# Requirements Document

## Introduction

The user's request, verbatim (2026-10-09):

> Create spec workflow MCP specifications. One specification for converting one of the standalone diagram tools to FBL and DISL. i.e. analyse the current implementation, define the DISL and FBL and then write the specification on the refactoring., also focus on finding issues and aspects where the DISL and FBL languages do not yet cover everything.

This is one of the fifteen specifications that reading gives (the series and the survey behind it are in `causal-loop-disl-fbl`, *Introduction*). It converts the **supply chain diagram** (`etalii/supply-chain`, `.supply`), a tool that is on neither language today.

**What "converted" means here** is what it means for the hype cycle graph: the toolbox, context menus, property rows, findings and refusals are derived from a bundled DISL definition by `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Disl`, the body is read and written through an FBL binding by `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl`, and the module keeps code only for what neither language can state. Nothing a user sees or a file holds changes unless this document names the change and the user has ruled on it.

**Why this tool is worth the analysis.** Its format is ADP's own YAML, the same family as the hype cycle graph and the timeline, so most of the conversion follows a pattern that exists. Three things do not: a node's group is a **key that names the group**, where both languages know containment only as nesting; the seven stages are **one key with legacy spellings**, where the draft definition makes them seven types; and the positions are **in the body**, with no registration layout at all. A DISL draft exists in etalii.adp; no FBL binding exists, so one is drafted in the appendix.

## What was measured

Read on 2026-10-09: the module at `develop` `9a646009`; `definitions/diagrams/supply-chain.dis` and `.md`, the DISL specification (0.3 draft) and the FBL specification (0.2 draft) in etalii-adp/etalii.adp at `develop` `da64ff0`; the two libraries in this repository; and the hype cycle graph module as the pattern.

| Thing | State |
| --- | --- |
| The module's backend | 3,565 lines of C# in 42 files. `SupplyChainParser` (234 lines) reads with YamlDotNet; `SupplyChainWriter` (321) writes through the shared `LineSplice`; `SupplyChainValidator` (104), `SupplyChainContextActionProvider` (293), `SupplyChainContextPropertyProvider` (180) and `SupplyChainToolboxProvider` (57) hold the findings, menus, rows and palette as code. `SupplyChainLayout` (446) and `SupplyChainTrace` (146) hold the layout and the highlight. 11 test files, 1,308 lines, six fixtures. |
| The module's client | 1,350 lines of TypeScript and CSS. `SupplyChainCanvas.tsx` (518) holds a hand-written canvas definition; it calls neither `parseDisl` nor `compileNotation`. |
| The DISL definition | Exists in etalii.adp, 864 lines, **written against DISL 0.1**. It is not bundled here (`src/diagrams/supply-chain/definition/` does not exist). It declares `persistence.format` as the plugin `net.etalii.adp.etalii.supply`, not as FBL. |
| The FBL binding | None, in either repository. The eight example bindings of `specifications/fbl/` do not include this tool. |
| The real-file check | None. `RealFiles/divergences.json` has no entry for this tool, and `ModuleCrossCheck.Tests` does not read a `.supply`, because there is no binding to read it through. |
| A parity transcript | None. The module has no `Parity/` folder. |
| The registration | Two lines, the origin and `body:`. No example and no fixture has a `layout:` block: positions are the keys `x` and `y` of the body. |

**How each finding below is known** is marked, because none of them was run: *read* is a reading of the code or the definition against the specification text; *recorded* is a sentence in the module's code or its companion document that already says so; *measured* is a search of the repositories whose command is in *Sources*. Requirement 1 turns every *read* finding into a fixture before anything is changed, so that each is either seen to happen or struck.

## Findings

The three kinds are those of `causal-loop-disl-fbl`: a **definition defect** is repaired in the definition or the binding, a **runtime gap** in this repository's libraries, a **language gap** in etalii-adp/etalii.adp. A **behaviour change to rule on** is an open question.

### A. The DISL definition against the module

| # | Finding | Kind | Known |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | The definition is DISL 0.1 (`"disl": "0.1"`). The client's `parseDisl` refuses anything but 0.3, and every bundled definition here is 0.3. It must be rewritten at 0.3 before it can be bundled. | Definition defect | Measured |
| A2 | Its companion document lists ten "DISL 0.1 gaps this diagram exposed". DISL 0.2 and 0.3 have answered seven: reading the selection (`view.selected`, 12.2), anchor sides restricted to left and right (`AnchorSpec.sides`), a pinned bezier reach (`BezierSpec`), a deletion confirmation with a condition and a count (`Confirmation`, `count` and `threshold`), a menu on empty canvas (`diagram` in `contextMenus[].for`), a drop from the palette (`canvas` in a drop's `on`), and a form item that retypes (kind `type`, 7.5). The definition still works around each: a plugin function `traceOf`, a click tool, Arrange offered from two menus only. Three remain open (finding A10). | Definition defect | Read |
| A3 | `persistence` names a plugin, with `newline`, `files`, `ordering`, `omitDefaults`, `precision` and `definition`. With the binding it becomes `format: "fbl"` with `binding` and a `typeMap`, and DISL 11.2 forbids those keys beside it. `ids.strategy` is `nanoid`, "the nearest shape"; DISL 11.5.1 has the exact one since 0.2, `uuid-v4` with `encoding: "base36"`, and names it as this family's ShortGuid. `view.store` is `["bounds"]`, which says positions are view data in the registration; they are the body's `x` and `y`, so it is `[]`. | Definition defect | Read |
| A4 | The definition gives no wire ids. The module answers 15 action ids (`supply-chain.add.` with each of seven stages, and eight others), 9 property ids and 8 toolbox ids, stated once for the client in `supplyChainIds.ts`. An element's wire id is its stored id, bare, with no prefix. | Language gap, already ruled: wire ids stay an `x-` block (Peter, 2026-10-06, "Spec all but wire ids"). This definition gets an `x-supply-chain` block. | Read |
| A5 | **Seven types against one key.** The definition makes each stage a node type under an abstract `Stage`, and a change of stage a retype. The file has one `type` key per node, six legacy words that read as the stage each became, and an unknown word that is kept, reported and not drawn. Under FBL that is seven rules told apart by `when`, a node with an unknown word matches none and is read past in silence, and a retype in a declared binding is "a `remove` and an `add` of the element under its new type's rule" (FBL 6.4) where the module rewrites one line. FBL's `map` on one attribute states the legacy words exactly ("several wire values may map to one model value"), but DISL's `typeMap` gives one binding type one `as`. | Definition defect, or language gap, by Q2 | Read |
| A6 | **Membership is a key, containment is nesting.** A node names its group with `group:` and groups do not nest. The definition states membership as containment (`Group.children` allows `Stage`). FBL 5.5 makes an element a child of "the nearest enclosing entry", and a `typeMap` attribute maps to an attribute name, `source`, `target`, `id` or `null`. Nothing maps a reference key to the parent. | Language gap (Q5) | Read |
| A7 | **The trace cannot run on the standalone runtime.** With `view.selected` the highlight is CEL over `reachable` and `predecessors`, as the companion says. `DislCelLibrary` declares twelve element and diagram methods and refuses a definition that calls another; neither graph function is among them, and nothing in the library reads a selection. Until both exist `SupplyChainTrace` and `SupplyChainSelections` stay code. | Runtime gap | Measured |
| A8 | **Elements the tool does not draw and DISL must.** The tool does not draw an entry without an id ("A node has no id and is not drawn.") nor a second holder of an id ("only its first entry is drawn."). DISL 11.5.4 says of both that they "MUST be drawn" and treated as ephemeral. "First" also differs: the layout and the validator take groups, then nodes, then flows, whatever order the sections have in the file; DISL takes reading order, which under FBL is document order. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q4); the first half is a language gap if today's behaviour is kept | Read |
| A9 | **The order of findings.** The validator sorts every finding by line, ties in the order it made them. DISL 8.6 orders by reader, built-in and rule, and `constraints.order` by code and then by line. Neither gives one list by line across codes. | Language gap | Read |
| A10 | What the notation cannot state at 0.3, by the companion's list and not re-checked beyond a search of the specification: a band with a second, separately animated line along it; a label placed by the width of another label; a context tool placed under a flow's label; and a layout that respects a stored position only when both coordinates are stored. | Language gap | Recorded (`supply-chain.md`, *Known gaps*) |
| A11 | **Six sentences under one code.** `supply-chain.unreadable` carries the parser's own sentences: a missing header, a version that is not a number, another version, an unknown key ("the line is kept"), an unknown stage, a number that will not read ("was ignored"), an entry that is not a mapping, and a body that is not YAML, whose sentence ends in YamlDotNet's own message. The hype cycle's patterns answer the unknown key (an `unknownKeys` host attribute), the entry that is not a mapping (an `Unreadable` rule) and the header (a rule at the root, mapped `as: "diagram"`). The not-YAML sentence cannot be the same in two hosts. | Definition defect with known patterns; the last is a language gap, minor | Read |
| A12 | **Rounding.** Positions are written with `Math.Round`, which rounds a half to the even neighbour (10.5 becomes 10). DISL snaps and FBL's `decimals` round halves away from zero (11). | Behaviour change to rule on (Q1) | Read |
| A13 | **A drag that changes the group.** A node whose centre lands in another group's frame joins it, the smallest frame winning, and a group left empty is given its old frame's corner. DISL 0.3's parent placement chooses a parent by geometry for a new element only. A hook on `move` with a `reparent` action may state it; the frames it must read are the layout plugin's. | To confirm in design; else language gap | Read |
| A14 | The banded layered layout with its lanes, the viewport filter, and the payloads (`share`, `weight`, `lanes`, `trace`) are the host's and stay code. This is not a gap: DISL names the layout as a plugin and has no streaming model on purpose. | None | Read |

### B. The FBL binding against the module's parser and writer

There is no binding to compare, so these are the places where the drafted one (appendix) cannot say what the parser and the writer do.

| # | Finding | Kind | Known |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | **A value is the text it was written with.** The parser reads every scalar's text: a name written `12`, `yes`, `null` or `~` is that text, and so is an id. FBL's YAML reading types a plain scalar by the core schema. This is the timeline's finding B1 unchanged, and it blocks this conversion the same way. | Language gap | Read; recorded for the timeline (`TimelineDisl.cs`) |
| B2 | **A number is whatever .NET reads from the text.** `quantity: "50"` in quotes reads as 50; `0x10` and `.inf` are reported as not a number, where the core schema reads 16 and infinity; `quantity: lots` keeps the node, ignores the key and reports "`quantity: lots` is not a number and was ignored." FBL 7.4 makes a value that does not convert an unreadable entry that "produces no element" unless DISL's tolerant loading says otherwise. | Language gap (the same construct as B1, then a DISL `parse`) | Read |
| B3 | **A flow whose end names no node** is kept, not drawn, and reported once per missing end, with one sentence for an end that is absent and another for one that names nothing. FBL 5.4 creates no relation. The hype cycle's pattern answers it: the entry is read as an element with reference attributes and `typeMap` makes it a relation with an unset end, reported by `std.references` with `detail.end`. A flow from a missing node to itself is reported as a self-flow only; the two built-ins would report both. | Definition defect, with a known pattern | Read |
| B4 | **An id written twice.** Groups, nodes and flows share one id space, every later holder is reported, and an edit finds the first. FBL gives a stored id to one holder. The hype cycle's `storedId` host attribute answers it. | Definition defect, with a known pattern | Read |
| B5 | **A key written twice in one mapping.** YamlDotNet refuses the document, so the body opens empty and refuses every edit. FBL 7.4 reports `fbl.duplicate-key`, a warning, and binds the first. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q4) | Read |
| B6 | **The first entry of a new document.** A new body is the header and `groups: []`, `nodes: []`, `flows: []`. The writer opens `[]` into a bare key before it appends. FBL 4.3 makes a flow collection one value whose only writable span is the whole collection, and the splice catalogue of 6.1 names no operation that opens one. The library here does it all the same (`YamlFamily`, "An empty flow sequence … becomes a block sequence"), so the runtime is ahead of the text. The writer also accepts `[ ]`, and leaves a `[]` followed by a comment as it is and writes a block item under it. | Language gap (the specification is silent), no runtime gap | Measured |
| B7 | **What a changed value writes.** `LineSplice.SetKey` replaces the whole line with the key and a newly quoted value. That drops a trailing comment and the author's quotes, and a stage set over a legacy word writes the new word. FBL replaces the value's span in its own style, and its `map` keeps a wire value that already maps to the model value. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q1) | Read |
| B8 | **Where a new key goes.** A key the entry lacks is inserted directly after the entry's first line, so a first placement writes `x` and `y` between `id` and `type`. FBL writes it where `insert.keys` orders it. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q1) | Read |
| B9 | **What a removal takes.** The writer removes the lines of the entry and leaves a comment directly above it. FBL removes the entry's line span, which "extends upwards over its leading comments". | Behaviour change to rule on (Q1) | Read |
| B10 | **The indentation of a new entry** is copied from the **first** entry of its list, the gap after the dash included; FBL copies the **previous sibling** and does not say the gap is copied (the timeline's finding B7). They differ in a file that mixes indentation. | To settle by fixture | Read |
| B11 | **Quoting of new text.** The writer quotes a value holding any colon or hash; FBL only `: ` and ` #`. FBL also quotes `on`, `off`, `y`, `n` and a date; the writer does not. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q1) | Read |
| B12 | **Removing a group** removes the `group` key of every member and then the entry. A binding's `remove.cascade` removes entries that reference the removed one; it cannot clear a key in them. Under containment DISL's `children: "reparent"` would state it (finding A6). | Follows A6 | Read |
| B13 | **The writer finds keys and sections by the start of a line**, not by the parsed tree. A value that spans lines (a block scalar) is replaced or removed on its first line only, a line inside one that begins with a key's name is taken for the key, and an entry written as a flow mapping gets a block key under it. No fixture has any of these. | Module defect, repaired by the conversion; to fix on purpose with its own guard (Q6) | Read |
| B14 | **A missing section** is created at the end of the document with its first entry, which `insert.create` with `end-of-document` states. A body whose root is not a mapping opens empty with no finding and accepts edits. | To settle by fixture | Read |

### C. Language gaps, as they would be reported to etalii-adp/etalii.adp

1. **FBL: a slot that reads a YAML scalar as written** (B1, B2). The timeline reports the same; this tool adds numbers, where the text decides and not the core schema. This one blocks the conversion.
2. **DISL and FBL: containment stated by a reference key** (A6, B12). Candidate: a `typeMap` attribute mapped to `"parent"`, with a parent that names nothing kept at the top level and reported as a dangling end is.
3. **DISL: an element with no id, or with an id an earlier element holds, that is not drawn** (A8). DISL 11.5.4 requires drawing it.
4. **DISL: findings in one list by line** (A9).
5. **FBL: opening an empty flow collection** (B6), which the library does and the specification does not say; and what a `set` does to an entry written as a flow mapping (B13).
6. **FBL: one binding type read as several model types by the value of a key, retyped in place** (A5), if Q2 keeps seven types; and what `map` reads for a wire value it does not list.
7. **FBL: a removal that leaves leading comments, and a new key placed after the first line** (B8, B9), only if Q1 rules that today's bytes are kept.
8. **DISL: the four notation gaps of A10**, and a move that reparents by where the centre lands (A13) if the design finds no hook that states it.
9. **DISL and FBL: the parser's own message in the sentence of `std.unparseable`** (A11).

These are candidates. Requirement 10 says they are recorded with their evidence and reported, and never worked around silently.

## Open questions

Each is put to the user as a selection. The option marked **(default)** is what this document is written against until the user rules otherwise.

| # | Question | Options | Criteria affected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 | When an edit changes one value, adds one key or removes one entry, what is written? | **(default) What FBL writes**: the value's own span in its own style, a new key where the binding orders it, a removed entry with the comment above it, halves rounded away from zero; a trailing comment and the author's quotes survive, and the transcript's edit hunks are regenerated once and reviewed as a diff. · **What the writer writes today**: the transcript stays byte-identical, and FBL needs a whole-line rewrite, a key placed after the first line and a removal that leaves comments, which are language changes first. · Other. | 5.2, 5.3, 1.4 |
| Q2 | Seven stage types or one? | **(default) One node type with a `stage` attribute**, an enumeration whose values carry the colour (DISL 0.3) and whose binding `map` carries the six legacy words; a change of stage is a changed value, as today. · **Seven types, as the draft has them**: a change of stage is a retype, which a declared binding plans as a remove and an add until FBL can retype in place. · Other. | 2.1, 4.2, 5.4 |
| Q3 | Finding B1 blocks the conversion until FBL answers it. What happens meanwhile? | **(default) Whatever is ruled on the timeline's Q3**, since it is the same gap; that document's default is to report the gap and wait. · **Work around it here**: the module keeps a small reader of its own for the scalars FBL types, named as standing in for the gap. · Other. | 4.3 |
| Q4 | What the languages would add or change that the tool does not do today: drawing an entry with no id or a duplicate one, opening a body with a duplicated key, taking "first" in file order. | **(default) Switched off or held back in this conversion**, so what is drawn and reported is the same before and after, and each is raised afterwards as a small change of its own. · **Adopted now**, each named in the transcript's diff. · Other. | 3.3, 4.5 |
| Q5 | Membership is a key and the languages know only nesting (finding A6). | **(default) A reference attribute `group` on the node**, no containment: the frame stays the layout plugin's, the Group row is a reference field, and removing a group clears the key by a hook. · **Containment, as the draft has it**, which waits for the construct of gap 2. · Other. | 2.1, 5.5 |
| Q6 | The writer's defects of finding B13. | **(default) Fixed on purpose in this work**, each with a fixture and a test seen to fail against today's writer first. · **Left to the conversion**, which removes the writer, with no guard. · Other. | 5.9 |
| Q7 | Is the client's canvas definition in scope? | **(default) Yes**: compiled from the bundled definition with `compileNotation`, today's hand-written definition kept in a test as the oracle, and what finding A10 names stated in a `NotationBindings`. · **No**: backend only, and the client keeps its hand-written definition until a later specification. · Other. | 8 |

## Alignment with Product Vision

The product direction (2026-09-26) is that every tool is a markup definition interpreted by a core in each IDE, with code only where a definition cannot reach. This tool's notation and format are the repository owner's own, so nothing outside ADP constrains either: where a language cannot say what the tool does, the choice between changing the language and changing the tool is fully the owner's, and this document puts each such choice as a question. It follows `product.md`'s *Don't reinvent, integrate* and `structure.md`'s rule that a diagram type adds declarations and no core code: what the libraries lack (finding A7) is added to the libraries for every tool.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1: An oracle before any change

**User Story:** As the owner of the tool, I want what it answers today frozen before anything is converted, so that every later step is held to it rather than to somebody's memory of it.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the work starts THEN a parity transcript `Parity/supply-chain.transcript.json` SHALL be generated from today's hand-written code and committed before any provider, parser or writer is changed, in the shape of the timeline's: per document, the context menu of every element, of the empty canvas, of a placement, of a connect gesture and of an unknown id; the property rows of every element; the findings; the payload of every mapped element; and a scripted edit sequence with each step's answer and the hunks it made to the text.
2. The corpus SHALL be the module's two examples, their copies under `src/examples/diagrams/supply-chain/`, the six fixtures, and **one new fixture for each finding of tables A and B marked Read that concerns a file** (A5, A8, A9, A11, A12, B1 to B5, B7 to B14), written so that the finding either shows in the transcript or is struck from this document with the reason.
3. A test SHALL require today's code to reproduce the checked-in transcript byte for byte, and SHALL have been seen to fail against a deliberately changed sentence before it is trusted.
4. WHEN a later step changes the transcript THEN the change SHALL be one this document names (Q1, Q4, Q6), regenerated on purpose, and the diff of the checked-in file SHALL be the review of it. Any other difference is a regression.

### Requirement 2: The definition, at DISL 0.3, bundled

**User Story:** As a tool engineer, I want one definition of the supply chain diagram that every host runs, so that the standalone tool is the definition's and not a second opinion.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. `definitions/diagrams/supply-chain.dis` in etalii-adp/etalii.adp SHALL be rewritten at DISL 0.3, using the constructs finding A2 names in place of each workaround, with the stages as Q2 rules and membership as Q5 rules, and SHALL validate against the DISL schema in that repository's checks.
2. It SHALL declare `persistence.format` `fbl` with `binding` naming the module's binding (Requirement 4.1), a `typeMap`, the id strategy of finding A3 and `view.store` empty, and an `x-supply-chain` block mapping its tools, actions and properties to the wire ids the module uses today (finding A4).
3. Its companion `supply-chain.md` SHALL be rewritten to say what DISL 0.3 cannot express, which is the gaps of section C and whatever Requirement 10 adds, and nothing that 0.3 can. Its sentences about a branch that is not merged SHALL go.
4. The definition SHALL be bundled into `src/diagrams/supply-chain/definition/` by `src/diagrams/tools/bundle-disl.sh`, never edited here, embedded in the backend project, and held by a `BundledDefinition.Tests` like the other bundled modules'.
5. WHEN the bundled definition is loaded by `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Disl` THEN it SHALL load with no diagnostic of severity error.

### Requirement 3: Toolbox, menus, rows and findings are derived

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want the palette, the context menus, the property rows and the findings to come from the definition, so that changing the tool is changing one file.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The eight toolbox items, the context menu of every target, the property rows of every element, the deletion confirmation and the reason on every unavailable action SHALL be derived from the bundled definition through `ToolboxDerivation`, `ContextMenuDerivation` and `FormDerivation`, mapped to the wire ids of `x-supply-chain`, and the providers SHALL hand them out and compute none themselves.
2. Every sentence a user reads today SHALL be read unchanged: "Increase quantity" and "Increase volume", "The quantity is already zero.", "Rename product…", "Put in a new group…" with "A group needs a name.", "Removing this node also removes the 1 flow to or from it." and its plural, asked only when there is a flow, "There is nothing to arrange until this diagram has a node.", the Group row's "(none)" and its choices by name, and the Step row showing 1 when the entry states none.
3. The seven codes (`supply-chain.unreadable`, `missing-id`, `duplicate-id`, `dangling-flow`, `self-flow`, `unknown-group`, `empty-group`) SHALL be derived by `ConstraintEvaluator` with today's severities, sentences and line locations; and no finding the tool does not give today SHALL appear, nor any element be drawn that is not drawn today (Q4).
4. WHERE DISL cannot give the findings in today's order (finding A9) THEN the order SHALL come from module code that sorts the derived list by line, named in the companion document as standing in for a language gap.
5. WHEN the derived answers are compared with the transcript of Requirement 1 THEN the menus, rows, findings and payloads SHALL be byte-identical.
6. The hand-written providers' logic SHALL be kept in the test project as the oracle (`Parity/HandWrittenSupplyChain.cs`), as the hype cycle keeps `HandWrittenGhg`, and removed from the product code.

### Requirement 4: The body is read through the binding

**User Story:** As a user, I want every `.supply` that opens today to open the same, read by the binding instead of by a parser only this host has.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The module SHALL own its binding, `backend/EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.SupplyChain/supply-chain.fbl`, embedded in the backend project, as the hype cycle owns its own, and the binding SHALL be offered to etalii.adp as the ninth example of `specifications/fbl/`.
2. WHEN a body is read THEN the groups, nodes and flows the binding reads SHALL be those `SupplyChainParser` reads today, for every document of the corpus of Requirement 1.2, a legacy stage word read as the stage it became and an unknown one kept and reported with today's sentence.
3. Every text SHALL be read as it was written, and every number as .NET reads the scalar's text (findings B1 and B2), by the construct FBL gains for it (Q3).
4. A flow whose end names no node SHALL be kept, not drawn, and reported as `supply-chain.dangling-flow` with today's two sentences, once per missing end; an id written more than once SHALL be reported on every later holder, and an edit SHALL find the first (findings B3 and B4).
5. An unknown key, an entry that is not a mapping, a number that will not read and the three header cases SHALL each be reported with today's sentence on today's line (finding A11), and a body with a duplicated key SHALL open as today (Q4).
6. Reading SHALL never throw on content, and a body that is not YAML SHALL open empty and refuse every edit. WHERE the sentence cannot carry YamlDotNet's message any more THEN the new sentence SHALL be named in the transcript's diff.

### Requirement 5: Every edit is written by splices

**User Story:** As a user editing a file I also edit by hand, I want an edit to change what I changed and nothing beside it.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every command of the module SHALL write through `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl` as a model change planned into splices; no module code SHALL build a line of YAML, and the module SHALL no longer use `LineSplice`.
2. WHEN a value changes THEN only its span SHALL change, in its own style (Q1): a trailing comment on its line and the author's quotes SHALL survive.
3. WHEN a key is added THEN it SHALL go where the binding's `keys` order puts it, and WHEN an entry is added THEN its indentation SHALL be that of the entries already there (finding B10); the first entry SHALL be addable to a new document and to a document that lacks the section (findings B6 and B14).
4. A change of stage SHALL write the stage's current word over whatever the line held, as today, or the difference SHALL be in the regenerated transcript (finding B7, Q2).
5. Removing a node SHALL remove the flows that name it, and removing a group SHALL remove the `group` key of its members and leave them where they are (finding B12), each as one undo step; "Put in a new group…" SHALL write the group and the node's key as one.
6. Moving a node, moving a group with its members, and Arrange diagram SHALL write `x` and `y` into the body as one edit each, a node joining the group whose frame its centre lands in and a group left empty keeping its place (finding A13).
7. Every refusal SHALL keep today's sentence: "That id is already used in this diagram.", "A flow runs from one node to another.", "A node does not supply itself.", "These two are already connected by a flow in this direction.", the amount and step sentences, the stage and group sentences, "A group has no value of its own; its members do." and "That is no longer in this diagram."
8. Undo SHALL restore the body byte for byte through the host's shared restore command, and a document ADP did not change SHALL be written back byte-identical, the pair of line-ending fixtures and the one without a final newline included.
9. A value that spans lines, a line inside one that begins with a key's name, and an entry written as a flow mapping SHALL each be edited without damage or refused with a sentence, each with a test seen to fail against today's writer first (finding B13, Q6).

### Requirement 6: Positions

**User Story:** As an author who placed a node, I want it to open where I left it after the conversion.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. Positions SHALL stay the body's `x` and `y`, the top-left corner in whole units, read as placing an entry only when both are stated; no registration SHALL gain a `layout:` block.
2. A document whose nodes state no position, which is both examples, SHALL be drawn where the layout draws it today, element for element in the transcript's payloads.

### Requirement 7: What stays code, and why

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want the code that remains in the module to be exactly what the languages cannot state, each piece with its reason.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The module SHALL keep: the banded layered layout, the element mapper and the viewport filter, the session and the document store, the `.proto` payloads, the trace and its record of selections until Requirement 9.1 is met, and the stand-ins of Requirements 3.4 and 4.6.
2. `SupplyChainParser`, `SupplyChainWriter`, `SupplyChainValidator` and the logic of the three providers SHALL leave the product code. What Requirement 3.6 keeps as an oracle lives in the test project.
3. WHEN the conversion is complete THEN the definition's companion document SHALL list every remaining module class beside the gap or the host concern that keeps it, and a class with neither SHALL be removed.

### Requirement 8: The client

**User Story:** As a user, I want the canvas to look and behave as it does, drawn from the same definition the backend runs.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The client's canvas definition SHALL be compiled from the bundled definition with `parseDisl` and `compileNotation` (Q7), with what the library cannot read from it stated in a `NotationBindings`.
2. Today's hand-written definition SHALL be kept in a test as the oracle, and the compiled one SHALL draw the same markup for the corpus.
3. IF `compileNotation` cannot read something the definition states THEN it SHALL be added to the shared library for every module, named for its geometry, and SHALL NOT be written in this module. What the definition cannot state (finding A10) SHALL stay in the module's client, named in the companion document.
4. A `tests.md` entry SHALL cover in a real browser, in both themes: the seven stage colours, a band's width following its volume, the goods moving and standing still when dimmed, a flow through its lanes, the trace up and down from a node, a flow and a group, the steppers and the `+` and `-` keys with the selection kept, dropping each of the eight toolbox entries, a node dragged into another group and out of its last one, inline rename of a node, a group and a product, and Arrange diagram with its undo.

### Requirement 9: The library work this tool needs

**User Story:** As a maintainer of the shared libraries, I want each thing this tool needs added once, for every tool.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Disl` SHALL implement `reachable` and `predecessors` as DISL 12.2 defines them and a `view.selected` the host supplies, and every other function the rewritten definition calls and `DislCelLibrary` lacks (finding A7). Each SHALL be proven by a library test seen to fail first.
2. The derivations SHALL support the constructs of finding A2 that they do not support yet; the design SHALL list which, from a load of the rewritten definition.
3. `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl` SHALL implement what FBL gains for findings B1 and B2, and SHALL otherwise need no change unless a fixture of Requirement 1.2 shows a defect in it; a language gap is not repaired here (Requirement 10).
4. No module name SHALL appear in a library change.

### Requirement 10: Gaps are recorded and reported, never tuned away

**User Story:** As the owner of DISL and FBL, I want every place the languages fall short reported back with its evidence, so that the languages are fixed where they are written.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every language gap found, the nine of section C and any the implementation adds, SHALL be recorded in the definition's companion document with the construct concerned, the evidence (a fixture or a test), and what would resolve it.
2. A gap SHALL NOT be closed by weakening a check, skipping a fixture, or stating in the definition something the tool does not do.
3. The delivery report SHALL list every gap as a candidate change for etalii-adp/etalii.adp, and every definition defect that was repaired.
4. WHEN a *read* finding of this document turns out not to occur THEN it SHALL be struck here with the fixture that shows it, as a small amendment.

### Requirement 11: Documentation, catalog and gates

**User Story:** As a reader of the repository, I want its pages to stay true through the conversion.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. `src/diagrams/readme.md`'s list of modules with a `definition/` folder, `docs/creating-a-diagram-module.md`, `docs/diagram-module-client-api.md`'s list of modules that compile their notation, and `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/solution-structure.md` where a sentence becomes false SHALL be updated in the change that makes them so.
2. `docs/tools.md`'s row for `etalii/supply-chain` SHALL name this specification.
3. All four gates SHALL exit zero on every pull request of this specification, judged by captured exit codes, and a newly created worktree SHALL be built before a green gate is trusted about the bundled definition.
4. WHEN the tasks document is written THEN every acceptance criterion here SHALL be claimed by a task, established by diffing the two sets, and two traces SHALL be read back to their artefacts.

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity

- The module ends as declarations, a binding, and the code Requirement 7.1 names. Library additions are named for what they do, never for this tool.
- The house rules apply: `src/.editorconfig`, no blocking call in an `async` method, `TestContext.Current.CancellationToken` in tests, no unneeded `using`, CRLF in the working tree; `.supply` and `.dis` are byte-compared and already `-text`, and `.fbl` in the module follows what the hype cycle's has.

### Performance

- Opening, validating, editing and arranging the largest `.supply` of the corpus (482 lines) SHALL not be perceptibly slower than today; an arrangement that writes every node SHALL be planned as one edit, as the hype cycle's is.

### Reliability

- No file that opens today opens differently (Requirement 4.2). An unchanged document is written back byte-identical and undo restores bytes (Requirement 5.8).
- Every test written for a finding is seen to fail against that finding before it is trusted.

### Usability

- Every sentence a user reads today is read unchanged (Requirements 3.2, 5.7), unless this document names the change.

## Out of scope

- Any change to what the tool does beyond the seven questions above.
- Changing DISL or FBL. Gaps are reported (Requirement 10); a language change is etalii.adp's own specification.
- The other tools of the series.
- The layout's algorithm and the viewport streaming model.

## Appendix: the binding, as drafted

A draft against FBL 0.2, `yaml` family, after the hype cycle's. One thing in it is **not valid FBL 0.2**: `"as": "text"`, which marks every slot that needs the construct of findings B1 and B2 and stands for gap 1. Everything else is meant to be valid. Flows are elements with reference attributes (finding B3), every entry carries `storedId` and `unknownKeys` (findings B4 and A11), one rule reads all seven stages through `map` (Q2), and `group` is a reference and not a `parent` (Q5).

```json
{
  "fbl": "0.2",
  "bindings": {
    "supply": {
      "title": "Supply chain diagram",
      "claims": { "extensions": [".supply"], "origins": ["etalii/supply-chain"] },
      "body": { "kind": "file", "family": "yaml" },
      "reader": "declared",
      "text": { "newline": "crlf", "indent": 2, "sequenceIndent": "indented", "finalNewline": true, "quote": "double" },
      "elements": [
        {
          "name": "document", "type": "Document", "at": "/",
          "readOnly": "The document's version is changed in the file itself.",
          "attributes": { "version": { "key": "supply-chain", "as": "text" } }
        },
        {
          "name": "group", "type": "Group", "at": "/groups/*", "when": "entry.all(k, true)",
          "id": { "from": { "key": "id" } },
          "attributes": {
            "storedId": { "key": "id", "as": "text", "readOnly": true },
            "unknownKeys": { "value": "entry.filter(k, !(k in ['id', 'name', 'description', 'x', 'y']))" },
            "name": { "key": "name", "as": "text", "empty": "keep" },
            "description": { "key": "description", "as": "text", "empty": "remove" },
            "x": { "key": "x", "as": "text", "number": { "decimals": 0 }, "empty": "remove" },
            "y": { "key": "y", "as": "text", "number": { "decimals": 0 }, "empty": "remove" }
          },
          "insert": { "place": "after-last", "container": "/groups", "create": { "at": "end-of-document" }, "keys": ["id", "name", "description", "x", "y"] },
          "remove": {}
        },
        {
          "name": "node", "type": "Node", "at": "/nodes/*", "when": "entry.all(k, true)",
          "id": { "from": { "key": "id" } },
          "attributes": {
            "storedId": { "key": "id", "as": "text", "readOnly": true },
            "unknownKeys": { "value": "entry.filter(k, !(k in ['id', 'type', 'name', 'description', 'group', 'quantity', 'unit', 'step', 'x', 'y']))" },
            "stage": { "key": "type", "as": "text", "map": { "source": "source", "processor": "processor", "producer": "producer", "integrator": "integrator", "hub": "hub", "outlet": "outlet", "consumer": "consumer", "raw-material": "source", "supplier": "processor", "manufacturer": "producer", "assembler": "integrator", "distributor": "hub", "retailer": "outlet" } },
            "name": { "key": "name", "as": "text", "empty": "keep" },
            "description": { "key": "description", "as": "text", "empty": "remove" },
            "group": { "key": "group", "as": "text", "empty": "remove", "reference": { "to": ["group"], "by": "storedId" } },
            "quantity": { "key": "quantity", "as": "text", "number": { "decimals": 4 }, "empty": "remove" },
            "unit": { "key": "unit", "as": "text", "empty": "remove" },
            "step": { "key": "step", "as": "text", "number": { "decimals": 4 }, "empty": "remove" },
            "x": { "key": "x", "as": "text", "number": { "decimals": 0 }, "empty": "remove" },
            "y": { "key": "y", "as": "text", "number": { "decimals": 0 }, "empty": "remove" }
          },
          "insert": { "place": "after-last", "container": "/nodes", "create": { "at": "end-of-document" }, "keys": ["id", "type", "name", "description", "group", "quantity", "unit", "step", "x", "y"] },
          "remove": { "cascade": ["flow"] }
        },
        {
          "name": "flow", "type": "Flow", "at": "/flows/*", "when": "entry.all(k, true)",
          "id": { "from": { "key": "id" } },
          "attributes": {
            "storedId": { "key": "id", "as": "text", "readOnly": true },
            "unknownKeys": { "value": "entry.filter(k, !(k in ['id', 'from', 'to', 'product', 'description', 'volume', 'unit', 'step']))" },
            "from": { "key": "from", "as": "text", "reference": { "to": ["node"], "by": "storedId" } },
            "to": { "key": "to", "as": "text", "reference": { "to": ["node"], "by": "storedId" } },
            "product": { "key": "product", "as": "text", "empty": "remove" },
            "description": { "key": "description", "as": "text", "empty": "remove" },
            "volume": { "key": "volume", "as": "text", "number": { "decimals": 4 }, "empty": "remove" },
            "unit": { "key": "unit", "as": "text", "empty": "remove" },
            "step": { "key": "step", "as": "text", "number": { "decimals": 4 }, "empty": "remove" }
          },
          "insert": { "place": "after-last", "container": "/flows", "create": { "at": "end-of-document" }, "keys": ["id", "from", "to", "product", "description", "volume", "unit", "step"] },
          "remove": {}
        },
        { "name": "group-not-a-mapping", "type": "Unreadable", "at": "/groups/*", "readOnly": "This entry is not a mapping, so it is kept as it is." },
        { "name": "node-not-a-mapping", "type": "Unreadable", "at": "/nodes/*", "readOnly": "This entry is not a mapping, so it is kept as it is." },
        { "name": "flow-not-a-mapping", "type": "Unreadable", "at": "/flows/*", "readOnly": "This entry is not a mapping, so it is kept as it is." }
      ],
      "registration": { "createOnFirstPlacement": false },
      "template": { "text": "supply-chain: 1\r\ngroups: []\r\nnodes: []\r\nflows: []\r\n" }
    }
  }
}
```

It declares no `header`, so that the three header cases keep the tool's own sentences from rules over the diagram's `version` and `fbl.header-mismatch` is not added to them. Four things are the design's to close with fixtures: what `map` reads for `type: quarry`, which it does not list (gap 6); whether the three `Unreadable` rules may each carry the tool's sentence, which names the list ("A node entry is not a mapping and was passed over."); that the template's three `[]` open as finding B6 says; and that a number slot marked for text still writes by `decimals`.

## Appendix: the definition's persistence and wire ids, as drafted

The rest of the definition is the existing file brought to 0.3 (Requirement 2.1). These two blocks are new, and both are meant to be valid DISL 0.3, because the default of Q5 keeps `group` an attribute. Under Q5's second option the node's entry would read `"attributes": { "group": "parent" }`, which is **not valid DISL 0.3** and is gap 2.

```json

  "persistence": {
    "format": "fbl",
    "binding": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etalii-adp/etalii.adp.ide.standalone/develop/src/diagrams/supply-chain/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.SupplyChain/supply-chain.fbl#supply",
    "ids": { "strategy": "uuid-v4", "encoding": "base36", "stable": true, "missing": "ephemeral" },
    "view": { "store": [] },
    "typeMap": {
      "Document": { "as": "diagram" },
      "Group": { "as": "Group", "hostAttributes": ["storedId", "unknownKeys"] },
      "Node": { "as": "Stage", "hostAttributes": ["storedId", "unknownKeys"] },
      "Flow": { "as": "Flow", "attributes": { "from": "source", "to": "target" }, "hostAttributes": ["storedId", "unknownKeys"] },

  },

      "processor": { "id": "supply-chain.toolbox.processor", "drop": "supply-chain.add.processor" },
      "producer": { "id": "supply-chain.toolbox.producer", "drop": "supply-chain.add.producer" },

      "consumer": { "id": "supply-chain.toolbox.consumer", "drop": "supply-chain.add.consumer" },
      "group": { "id": "supply-chain.toolbox.group", "drop": "supply-chain.add-group" }
    },
    "actions": {
      "editLabel": "supply-chain.rename",
      "delete": "supply-chain.remove",
      "increase": "supply-chain.increase",
      "decrease": "supply-chain.decrease",
      "putInNewGroup": "supply-chain.group",
      "arrange": "supply-chain.arrange",

      "addGroupHere": "supply-chain.add-group",
      "addSourceHere": "supply-chain.add.source",
      "addProcessorHere": "supply-chain.add.processor",
      "addProducerHere": "supply-chain.add.producer",
      "addIntegratorHere": "supply-chain.add.integrator",
      "addHubHere": "supply-chain.add.hub",
      "addOutletHere": "supply-chain.add.outlet",
      "addConsumerHere": "supply-chain.add.consumer"
    },

      "name": "supply-chain.name",
      "stage": "supply-chain.stage",

      "quantity": "supply-chain.quantity",
      "product": "supply-chain.product",
```

One action id serves three element types and two attributes: `supply-chain.rename` edits a node's or a group's `name` and a flow's `product`, and `supply-chain.group` is both an action id and a property id. The shape of `x-ghg` allows both. The draft's existing `x-supplyChain` keys, which hold each type's document spelling and legacy words, go: the binding's `map` holds them.
